c133.title: Two Weeks in Tokyo
c133.story: Max spent two weeks with his friend Kenji in Tokyo. On the first night, they ate [[sushi]] near the station. The next day, they had hot [[ramen]] for lunch. Max bought three [[manga]] books for his little sister. In the park, he saw a woman in a beautiful [[kimono]]. Later, a [[geisha]] walked slowly under the pink [[sakura]] trees. At dinner, Max did not know the table [[etiquette]]. Kenji's [[senpai]] showed him how to hold chopsticks. On the last weekend, a [[typhoon]] hit the city. They stayed inside, played games and laughed all day.

c134.title: Backpacking in Asia
c134.story: Anna's friend Lisa went backpacking in Asia last summer and slept in cheap [[hostels|hostel]]. In Seoul, she ate [[kimchi]] with two girls who loved K-pop. When their favorite singer walked on stage, they screamed, "[[Oppa|oppa]]!" In China, she had pork [[bao]] for breakfast and a sweet [[mandarin]] after it. The whole meal cost only twenty [[yuan]]. In Vietnam, she rented a [[moped]] and paid for it in [[dong]]. In Thailand, a market woman sold her fruit for a hundred [[baht]]. Lisa tried [[durian]], but the smell was too strong for her. She liked the [[papaya]] much more. Before her trip, a doctor gave her pills against [[malaria]], just in case. Lisa came home tired, happy, and full of stories.

c135.title: A Wedding in India
c135.story: Anna's college friend Priya invited her to a wedding in India. All the women wore bright [[saris|sari]], and Anna wore a borrowed one too. Priya's grandfather wore a white [[dhoti]], and her uncle wore a red [[turban]]. The uncle is a [[Sikh]], and he loves telling old stories. He told Anna about a rich [[raja]] who lived in a golden palace. In the story, a foreign visitor made the servants call him [[sahib]]. After lunch, a snake charmer showed the guests a [[cobra]] in a basket. In the evening, the family went to the temple for a [[puja]]. An old [[mystic]] read prayers in [[Sanskrit]] with his eyes closed. At the end, he gave everyone sweet [[prasad]]. Anna said it was the most beautiful day of her year.

c136.title: Istanbul, Dubai and Cairo
c136.story: Max's parents took a long trip around the Middle East this spring. In Istanbul, they went shopping in an old [[bazaar]]. Max's mom paid two hundred [[lira]] for a small blue [[amulet]] for Max. A guide told them about a [[pasha]] who ruled the city long ago. In Dubai, they visited a palace where a [[sheikh]] once welcomed guests. The guide explained that Dubai is the biggest city of its [[emirate]]. On a short stop in Jordan, they paid for a taxi in [[dinars|dinar]]. Then they rode camels across the desert to a green [[oasis]]. On the way, Max's dad saw a lake, but it was only a [[mirage]]. In the morning, a [[scorpion]] was sleeping in his shoe! In Cairo, they heard a [[mullah]] lead the morning prayers at an old mosque. They saw the Great [[Sphinx|sphinx]] and took a boat trip to the Nile [[delta]].

c137.title: A Safari in Kenya
c137.story: Anna's aunt Olena always wanted to see wild animals. Her [[travel agent]] found her a cheap [[safari]] in Kenya. Kenya lies right on the [[equator]], so it was hot every day. Olena had never been to the [[tropics]] before. It was her first time on another [[continent]], too. On the first night, she heard a [[hyena]] laughing in the dark. In the morning, a young [[gazelle]] ran past her jeep. The wide [[savanna]] looked golden in the sun. At a village market, she paid fifty [[shillings|shilling]] for a jar of [[shea]] butter. Then she flew to South Africa and changed her money into [[rand]]. She came home with a suntan and a thousand photos.

c138.title: Max in Latin America
c138.story: Max traveled to Mexico, where his new friend Diego met him at the bus station. "Welcome, [[amigo]]!" Diego said, and he paid for the taxi with two hundred [[pesos|peso]]. In the evening, Diego's uncles drank [[tequila]] at a small cafe. Max ordered a [[margarita]] without alcohol and watched the sun set behind a tall [[cactus]]. A week later, the two friends flew to Peru. In the mountains, a [[llama]] carried their heavy bags. Their guide said a [[puma]] sometimes walks near this trail. High above them, a huge [[condor]] flew in slow circles. They passed small farms where [[coca]] grows on green hills. In the Amazon jungle, the guide cut a path with a [[machete]]. A [[caiman]] watched them quietly from the river bank. The guide said the river was full of [[piranhas|piranha]], so Max stayed in the boat.

c139.title: Summer Down Under
c139.story: Anna's cousin Dan got a summer job at a beach [[resort]] in Australia. On his first day off, he saw a [[kangaroo]] jumping across the road. In a tall tree, a sleepy [[koala]] did not even open its eyes. Near the forest, a wild [[dingo]] watched him and then ran away. A local boy taught Dan how to throw a [[boomerang]]. For dinner, they ate fresh [[crab]] on the beach. Dan slept in a small [[bungalow]] by the sea. One night, a strong [[cyclone]] hit the coast, but his little house stayed safe. On a small island nearby, tourists in bright [[bikinis|bikini]] read a sign: "No [[topless]] sunbathing." A wooden [[tiki]] stood at the door of the beach bar. Far away, red [[lava]] glowed at the top of an old volcano. In the evening, Dan played the [[ukulele]] for his new friends by the fire.

c140.title: A Week in New York
c140.story: Anna and Max spent a week in New York in October. Their hotel was [[downtown]], near a wide [[boulevard]]. A huge [[billboard]] over the street showed a smiling cat. On the first evening, they ate dumplings in [[Chinatown]]. On Sunday morning, they went to [[brunch]] at a small cafe. Anna ate a warm [[bagel]] with [[cream cheese]]. Max had a big plate of [[French toast]]. On the way back, Anna found a [[dime]] on the street. "It's lucky money!" she said and laughed. On their last night, they had dinner with Max's cousin Ben. Max ordered a [[steak]], and Anna tried [[lobster]] for the first time. Then they watched the city lights from Ben's [[penthouse]].

c141.title: Dad's Small Bakery
c141.story: Last year, Anna's dad decided to become a [[businessman]]. He opened a small bakery with his old friend Taras, who became his [[business partner]]. First, they wrote a [[business plan]], and Anna helped them check the [[cash flow]] every week. After six months, the bakery made its first small [[profit]]. They kept their [[pricing]] simple: every pie cost the same. They chose a local [[vendor]] for flour and sugar. Soon a big [[retailer]] wanted to sell their bread in its stores. Taras had worked in [[retail]] before, so he knew what to say. Then they hired a [[sales manager]] named Iryna. They also joined a farmers' [[cooperative]] to get fresh milk and eggs. Sometimes they even used [[barter]] and paid the farmers with fresh bread. Now a regional [[distributor]] takes their pies to five towns.

c142.title: Max's Startup
c142.story: Max and two friends started their own [[startup]] last spring. As the [[founder]], Max had to explain the idea to everyone. The [[concept]] was simple: an app that plans cheap, healthy meals for students. Their [[business model]] was a small monthly payment. Max showed a simple [[use case]]: a tired student opens the app and finds dinner. An [[investor]] named Mrs. Bondar listened carefully. She said the app could be a [[game changer]] for busy students. She offered them a [[win-win]] deal and asked to join their [[venture]]. She put in the [[capital]], and the team brought their [[know-how]]. Soon they got a [[patent]] for their smart shopping list. A local newspaper called Max a young [[innovator]]. His mom cut out the article and put it on the fridge.

c143.title: Anna's Marketing Seminar
c143.story: Anna is studying [[marketing]], and on Friday she went to a [[seminar]] at her university. The teacher gave the class a [[case study]] about a small juice company. The company had good juice but very weak [[branding]]. A real [[art director]] helped Anna's team create a new [[logo]] and a [[slogan]]. Then they talked about [[targeting]]: who should buy this juice? Anna's team wanted to sell it to the [[mass market]], not only to rich people. They read a survey, and most [[respondents|respondent]] liked the green bottles. They compared their sales numbers with a [[benchmark]] from a bigger company. Next, they learned about [[merchandising]] and where to put bottles in a store. Anna suggested a summer [[promotion]]: buy two bottles, get one free. Finally, they designed a simple [[landing page]] with the price and a big orange button. The teacher said their project was the best in the class.

c144.title: A Day at the Tech Expo
c144.story: Last weekend, Anna helped her friend at a big tech [[expo]] in Kyiv. The [[keynote]] was given by a famous [[businesswoman]] who started as a [[product manager]]. Every [[sponsor]] hung a bright [[banner]] above its stand. At the door, a young [[promoter]] handed Anna a [[flyer]] about a new book. The book, about smart robots, was already a [[bestseller]]. The [[PR]] team sent a [[press release]] to all the news sites at noon. Anna went to a short talk about [[email marketing]] for small shops. The speaker said she had worked in [[high-tech]] for twenty years. The most popular stand had an [[android]] that looked almost human. It smiled, shook Anna's hand and said, "Welcome to the future!" That evening, Anna told Max she wanted a job in [[high tech]] one day.
